[49016 Technology and Innovation Management | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject teaches you to manage technology and innovation within organisations, from inception to transfer. You'll learn to navigate the full product and service development cycle, including needs analysis, ideation, and implementation. Through an innovation project, you'll apply quantitative and qualitative tools to grasp and manage the intricate components of the innovation process, preparing you to design and analyse effective innovation strategies.

[49016 Technology and Innovation Management | Learning and teaching activities]
The subject consists of weekly 1-hour lecture (online) and 2-hours tutorial workshops.

Lectures (1 hour weekly): Each lecture introduces key concepts and theories in technology and innovation management. You will have opportunities to ask questions and engage in discussion.

Tutorial Workshops (2 hours weekly): These sessions are highly interactive and include:

- Class discussion and short presentations

- Group and individual problem-solving activities

- Project work and project presentations

Activities and assignments are designed to help you:

- understand core concepts and tools of technology and innovation management

- Apply these tools in real-world contexts through industry-relevant, experiential learning.

Collaboration and Feedback

You will work collaboratively on tasks that focus on applying concepts in different scenarios. Regular feedback will be provided during class activities and on assessment tasks to support your learning.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[49016 Technology and Innovation Management | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Identify and discuss the scope of technological change and innovation in organisations and markets from a social, environmental and financial perspective. (B.1)
SLO2: Analyse and design innovation processes and show how to deploy a customer focus. (C.1)
SLO3: Evaluate and use appropriate technology and innovation management tools. (D.1)
SLO4: Communicate appropriately with stakeholders on a new product or service using relevant documentation (E.1)
